search_log: Searched "True Believer" "Nicholas Sparks" with excerpt, first chapter, PDF excerpt, publisher, and Google Books terms; found and opened the author-hosted 39-page PDF and the permission-reprinted Bookreporter excerpt.

Searched the verified title and author with point of view, third person, narrator, perspective, and alternating point of view terms; no authoritative whole-book grammatical-person description was found.

Searched for epistolary, diary, frame narrative, multiple narrators, and alternating narration; found no evidence of sustained first- or second-person base sections. A StoryGraph review mentioned several character perspectives but did not identify a change in grammatical person.

Searched exact text from q01324 and q01354 to resolve their local boundaries. Results reproduced the Goodreads fragments but supplied no reliable attribution for q01354; broader interior text confirmed sustained third-person focalization elsewhere.
Rejected first-person search results concerning Virginia Euwer Wolff's different novel titled True Believer as a title collision, not evidence about Nicholas Sparks's book.

person_note: The controlling narration is third person with shifting character focalization, principally through Jeremy and Lexie rather than through a participating narrator. Goodreads passages q01329, q01331, q01335, q01342, and q01355 independently expose sustained third-person access to characters' inner states, while the authorized opening excerpt confirms the same narrative form across dozens of pages. The isolated first-person fragments q01324 and q01354 lack usable attribution or boundaries and are therefore treated as unresolved local speech, quotation, or clipping rather than autonomous base sections. No credible source indicates a sustained change of grammatical person; the remaining uncertainty concerns only those fragments' local provenance, not the book-level classification.
